claims.text: The starting materials are crystalline, near-equiatomic solid-solution nanoparticles containing five or more metals.
Introducing a minor alloying element with a strongly negative enthalpy of mixing can stabilize these nanoparticles during operation at 773–1173 K.
The minor alloying element reduces the nanoparticles' tendency toward phase separation.
The minor alloying element promotes a more homogeneous distribution of constituent elements.
Reduced phase separation and improved elemental homogeneity preserve the crystalline structure.
Reduced phase separation and improved elemental homogeneity prevent chemical instability.
Alloyed nanoparticles will have greater structural stability than otherwise identical nanoparticles without the minor alloying element.
Alloyed nanoparticles will have greater chemical stability than otherwise identical nanoparticles without the minor alloying element.
Improved structural and chemical stability will enhance catalytic performance.
Improved structural and chemical stability will increase catalyst longevity.
The intervention's effectiveness may depend on the identity and concentration of the minor alloying element and on the underlying nanoparticle composition.
The proposed operating boundary is 773–1173 K under prolonged exposure.
